name: rustyfi
description: Syntax highlighting, formatting, LSP and live Markdown preview for SATySFi documents, powered by the rustyfi compiler.

commands.title: rustyfi: Open Preview to the Side

rustyfi.serverPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `rustyfi` binary. When empty, the extension looks on `PATH`, then for `target/release/rustyfi` inside the open workspace.

rustyfi.lsp.enable.description: Run `rustyfi lsp` and attach the language client (diagnostics, hover, go-to-definition, completion, symbols).

rustyfi.trace.server.description: Trace the LSP traffic in the output channel.

enumDescriptions: Format by running `rustyfi fmt -` over the buffer (honours the rustyfi.format.* options below).
Let the language server's own formatting provider handle it (the rustyfi.format.* options below do not apply).
rustyfi.format.provider.markdownDescription: Who formats a SATySFi document. `rustyfi lsp` also advertises a formatting provider; leaving this at `cli` suppresses the server's so the two do not both register.

rustyfi.format.lang.markdownDescription: Passed as `--lang`. `auto` omits the flag, letting the formatter sniff each file's own generation.

rustyfi.format.maxWidth.markdownDescription: `--max-width`: line budget in display columns (a CJK character counts 2). `null` omits the flag, so `$RUSTYFI_FMT_MAX_WIDTH` or the built-in default (100) applies.

rustyfi.format.tabSpaces.markdownDescription: `--tab-spaces`: columns per indentation step. `null` omits the flag (built-in default 2).

rustyfi.format.maxBlankLines.markdownDescription: `--max-blank-lines`: consecutive blank lines kept. `null` omits the flag (built-in default 2).

rustyfi.format.wrapComments.markdownDescription: `--wrap-comments`: reflow an own-line `%` comment that reads as prose. `null` omits the flag (built-in default true).

rustyfi.format.wrapInlineText.markdownDescription: `--wrap-inline-text`: re-wrap the text inside `{ ... }`. `null` omits the flag (built-in default true). Set `false` for a corpus of one-sentence-per-line prose.

rustyfi.build.autoSave.markdownDescription: Save the document before building. A build that silently compiles the last saved bytes defeats its own purpose; turn this off and a dirty document refuses instead.

rustyfi.build.timeout.markdownDescription: Milliseconds before a build is abandoned. Higher than the preview's, because a build is deliberate and a long document is allowed to take its time.

enumDescriptions: The real page, laid out by the same engine the build uses.
A reflowed, semantic reading: no pages, but it wraps to the panel.
rustyfi.preview.format.markdownDescription: What the preview renders. `pdf` is what the build produces, rendered page by page with pdf.js — the default, and the only mode that shows real layout. `markdown` reflows the document to the panel width and is easier to read while writing prose; pair it with `#rustyfi.preview.mathMode#` (`svg-outline-math` reproduces equations exactly).

rustyfi.preview.mathMode.markdownDescription: How equations are written in the preview. **Markdown mode only** — a PDF is typeset by the engine, so there is nothing to re-express. `unicode-math` writes them as their characters in reading order (x², ∑ₐᵇ) — plain text that always renders. The others are passed straight through to the compiler; `katex` and `mathml` emit markup this preview does not typeset, so they will show as source.

rustyfi.preview.debounce.markdownDescription: Milliseconds of typing quiet before the preview recompiles. The default 300 was chosen from measured compile times on this repo's corpus (0.13–0.22 s typical, ~4 s worst case); see the README.

rustyfi.preview.enable.description: Allow the preview panel to recompile automatically as you type. When false, the preview only refreshes on the explicit refresh command.

rustyfi.preview.timeout.markdownDescription: Milliseconds before an in-flight preview compile is killed.

rustyfi.libRoot.markdownDescription: Passed as `--lib-root` to preview compiles. Empty uses the compiler's own discovery (`$RUSTYFI_LIB_ROOT`, then `lib-rustyfi/` above the document, and so on).
